item.title: How to use optional chaining in JavaScript
item.description: Using optional chaining in JavaScript safely accesses nested object properties and methods without throwing errors when intermediate values are null or undefined. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve used optional chaining extensively for API response handling, configuration access, and defensive programming. From my expertise, the most reliable approach is using the ?. operator to chain property access with automatic null checking at each level. This ES2020 feature eliminates verbose null checking code while providing safe navigation through complex object structures.
